customer_julia: Hi support — our org (acct 12345) shows 0 monthly credits after the month rollover. Customer says they should've refilled at 00:00 CET but APIs still return 429. Can you check?

alex_support: Thanks Julia. Can you confirm the tenant timezone and if you changed plans mid-cycle? Any request IDs or sample responses would help. :eyes:

customer_julia: Tenant TZ is CET. We did upgrade the plan on 2026-03-15 at 11:20 UTC (team -> business). Here are two failing request ids: rq_abc123, rq_def456. Sample response header from one call: `X-Credit-Remaining: 0`, `X-Next-Refill: 2026-04-01T00:00:00Z`. Body had standard 429.

alex_support: Got it. Two things to check: 1) whether proration on upgrade created a separate credit bucket that isn't surfaced to the org-level API, and 2) whether long-running streaming connections are reading a cached quota state. Devin, any quick theory?

devin_infra: Likely combination of both. Proration flow creates a "topup" bucket tied to the billing entity; the public credits endpoint returns the org-level bucket and not the prorated topup until the reconciliation job runs. Additionally, live streaming sockets maintain an in-memory quota snapshot and won't pick up the reconciled amount until the session restarts or the cache is invalidated.

devin_infra: Repro steps for infra: 1) simulate upgrade (POST /internal/billing/upgrade -> creates topup_job). 2) Call GET /v1/orgs/12345/credits (shows org bucket). 3) Call GET /internal/billing/topups/12345 (shows pending topup with status: pending). 4) Open long-lived websocket and stream tokens -> quota stays 0 until job completes or cache invalidated.

devin_infra: Quick workaround (admins only): `POST /admin/tenants/12345/invalidate_quota_cache` returns { "job_id": "job_789", "status": "queued" }. Once job_789 finishes the topup is merged and `GET /v1/orgs/12345/credits` will show the updated value.

mike_billing: Confirmed — proration creates a temporary top-up bucket while we calculate the rounded credits for the remainder of the billing period. That bucket is visible to billing APIs but not to the public `credits` endpoint until the merge job runs. If the customer upgraded shortly before the refill boundary, the topup's `next_refill` can be set to the next cycle (hence header you saw). We're going to fast-track job_789 for this tenant.

alex_support: Julia — short-term workarounds: 1) ask users to reconnect streaming sessions / restart notebook kernels to pick up reconciled credits, or 2) we can trigger the admin invalidate job for you (we'll do it now). I've escalated to billing to expedite the merge.

quota-bot: Admin job queued by alex_support: `job_789` status queued -> running

mike_billing: Job completed. `GET /v1/orgs/12345/credits` now returns { "available_credits": "120000", "unit": "tokens", "next_refill": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z" }. Please confirm customers can make requests again. :white_check_mark:

customer_julia: Confirmed — requests accepted now and streaming sessions that were restarted are working. Thank you all.

alex_support: Marking as resolved for now. Follow-up: billing will reconcile the proration edge-case to ensure topup visibility faster when upgrades happen within 24h of month boundary. Filed internal ticket ENG-PRORATE-142.

customer_julia: Appreciate it, closing on our side.
